thread:
tara: FYI after the mix-quant selector rollout we shipped this morning, we are seeing a small-but-consistent eval delta on the payments JSON output. some fields are getting reordered and occasional extra keys (payment_ref) appear in generated JSON.

matt: I can repro locally with model=redwood-mix-v2 quant_mode=fp8+int4, seq_len=2048, batching=adaptive. repro script: `./scripts/run_eval.sh --model mix-v2 --quant mix --batch-policy adaptive`. output attached below.

jess: thanks — looks like KV cache alignment diverges when kernel routing switches mid-request. i saw a 0.8% higher KV-miss rate on the mixed path. telemetry: `kv_miss_rate=0.008`, `kernel_switches=2`, `avg_latency_ms=98`.

kevin: can you paste the raw trace? last time kernel_switches mid-seq caused token offset misapply in the attention module.

matt: paste of minimal trace (truncated):
```
TRACE: dispatch_path=mix_selector->fp8_kernel
TRACE: kv_index=1245 expected_offset=8192 applied_offset=8176
TRACE: kernel_switch at token_idx=1024 from fp8->int4
OUTPUT: {"amount": 12.50, "currency": "USD", "payment_ref": "XYZ123"}
```

jess: that `applied_offset=8176` vs expected `8192` is the red flag. looks like kv cache compacting logic assumes single precision stride; when we switch to int4 kernels the byte-per-key changes and we aren't converting offsets.

tara: eval-bot ran the nightly regression set; summary: `eval-bot: run=nightly+mixquant, delta=+2.3% exact-match-drop on payments-schema, hallucination-rate +0.9%`. full report linked: https://internal/reports/evals/2812345678 (internal).

eval-bot: Note: failing prompt examples (n=12) all share long prefix with repeated system messages + tool call output before generation. sequence lengths around 1500-2200 tokens.

kevin: plausible cause: our kernel selection logic switches kernel variant based on upcoming sequence remainder to save compute, but it doesn't remap the per-block KV index when quantization bitwidth changes. we should either: 1) enforce no kernel switches mid-request for models with KV stride variance, or 2) make the KV index remapping explicit in the runtime transition.

matt: quick local experiment: forcing single kernel (`--force-kernel fp8`) fixes output: exact-match back to baseline, latency +3%. so mitigation path: pin kernel for canary traffic that uses payments templates.

jess: i started a branch `fix/kv-offset-conversion` to convert offsets on kernel switch. small patch: at switch time compute new_offset = round(old_offset * (old_stride / new_stride)). still running unit tests.

tara: can we do an emergency canary rollback for users hitting production anomalies? deploy-bot, rollback canary to previous kernel routing?

deploy-bot: Canary traffic for mix-quant-selector in us-west-2 rolled back to stable routing at 2812345820.

kevin: good. next steps: triage checklist —
- confirm repro cases and collect offending prompts (matt)
- finish offset conversion patch + unit tests (jess)
- add assertion in runtime: on kernel switch, verify kv_index roundtrip equality for sanity (kevin)
- consider temporary policy: disable mid-request kernel switches for pinned models (tara)

matt: i'll upload failing prompts to the shared drive and add CS tickets for customers who reported anomalies.

jess: tests passing locally, pushing PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3412

tara: thanks team. i'll schedule a short post-mortem after PR merges to decide whether to backport to dedicated/private distros.

kevin: also add a telemetry alert: if `kv_miss_rate` increases by >0.5% after routing change, auto-disable kernel switching for that model id.

matt: noted. re-checking perf: forcing fp8 increased avg token throughput -3% but resolved the hallucination. tradeoff seems acceptable for templates.

tara: cool. if nobody objects i'll mark this as active triage and we can close after PR merge + canary verification. :thumbsup:
